_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS ROUND 1090's GATE IS NOT VACUOUS — run it from the
The gate's own first run is the other half of the proof and it is already
recorded: pointed at this repository's live cache storage it answered 24.78
GB against a 10.00 GB budget and exited 1, and pointed at the tree BEFORE
this round's repair its two real-tree tests failed at 63.07 GB. What that
cannot show is whether `tests/law.rs` would notice if a mechanism stopped
working — a test over an injected population passes because the population
is wrong as easily as because the code is right. Each injection below
removes one mechanism and names the test that must go red for it.
Scoped to this crate's own suite: nothing here touches the tree it judges,
so running the repository's whole suite would be five minutes of proving

injections.name: the-gate-that-could-not-look-reports-a-finding
injections.why: R1129, AND IT WAS MEASURED SILENT BEFORE IT WAS FIXED. R1104 moved this gate's WORDS into the library so that a suite could read them, and left the EXIT CODES here: `2` when a refusal is `Unreached` — I could not look — and `1` when the caches themselves break the law. Those are two answers a hook acts on differently, and collapsing them is the failure R1078 named. Run against the suite as it stood, this went SILENT across fifty-two tests: moving the words was half the repair, and nothing ran the binary

injections.name: a-finding-about-the-caches-is-reported-as-a-broken-gate
injections.why: the other direction of the same collapse, and the one that reads as the gate being at fault rather than the repository: caches over budget are a finding a person can act on, and `2` says `do not believe what you just read`

injections.name: the-refusals-are-judged-but-never-said
injections.why: an exit code is one bit and this gate's findings are a distribution — which key, how large, how many absent. A run that returns 1 and prints nothing hands a person the fact that something is wrong and none of what it is

injections.name: the-clean-answer-is-an-exit-code-and-nothing-said
injections.why: a gate that prints only its findings cannot be told from one that never ran — the sentence on the clean path is what says the reading HAPPENED, and it is the line a person looks for in a green log

edits.from: println!("every cache this repository declares is one it keeps");

injections.name: what-was-reached-is-not-printed-before-it-is-judged
injections.why: the report is printed FIRST and unconditionally, because a gate that never opened anything and a gate that found nothing wrong print the same silence. Withholding it until after the verdict means the clean runs — the ones nobody reads closely — carry no evidence of what was read

injections.name: an-absent-cache-is-priced-from-anything-at-all
injections.why: every key in this repository holds `~/.cargo/registry`, so pricing an absent cache from any cache it merely OVERLAPS prices a 0.10 GB registry cache as a 3 GB build tree and invents demand that is not there — a gate turning red at a repository doing nothing wrong

injections.name: a-lower-bound-is-good-enough-to-pass
injections.why: this repository's registry cache is 0.10 GB and its build tree 3.06 GB, a factor of thirty, so an evicted `target` cache priced off the registry cache that survived it reads as well inside budget — a green verdict on exactly the failure this gate was built for

injections.name: a-cache-belongs-to-the-first-key-that-claims-it
injections.why: this repository's oldest key `Linux-cargo-` is a prefix of every other key in the file, so a join that is not most-specific-wins credits the small general job with the huge specific job's cache, leaves the specific one looking satisfied, and reports a third of the real demand

injections.name: a-repository-declaring-no-cache-is-simply-clean
injections.why: a reader that stopped recognising `actions/cache` hands the law an empty list, and an empty list satisfies every one of its clauses vacuously — the parser bug that reports the tidiest possible repository

injections.name: the-biggest-generation-under-a-key-is-the-one-judged
injections.why: a lockfile bump changes every key at once and leaves the previous generation held until it ages out, and the previous one is the BIGGER one whenever a repository has just made its caches smaller — so judging by size keeps this round's own repair red for the seven days that takes

injections.name: one-key-may-mean-two-different-things
injections.why: GitHub stores one archive per key, so two jobs declaring one key with different paths get whatever the first saver wrote; the workflow reads as though both were true and nothing else in this repository can see it

injections.name: a-row-is-a-declaration-rather-than-a-key
injections.why: two jobs naming one key share one entry in GitHub's storage and cost the budget once; counting per declaration prices a shared cache twice and refuses a repository for reading one cache from two places, which is what sharing a key is for

injections.name: a-cache-that-exists-is-a-job-that-was-warm
injections.why: `actions/cache` saves only when it did NOT find an exact hit, so a cache created inside this run is a job that restored nothing and rebuilt; without the clock comparison the gate reports a repository whose jobs each take half an hour as spotless, which is the verdict Round 1089 had to overturn by hand

injections.name: two-endpoints-two-spellings-compared-as-plain-strings
injections.why: the runs endpoint gives whole seconds and the caches endpoint gives nanoseconds; comparing them as text lands on the right answer only because `.` sorts below `Z`, and the day the runs endpoint gains a fractional part that accident stops holding and four hundred milliseconds decides a half-hour verdict

injections.name: a-dependency-bump-is-refused-like-any-other-cold-build
injections.why: a key hashing lockfiles that moved MUST be rebuilt, and refusing that makes every dependency change a red build — a gate that is red for a correct commit is one somebody switches off

injections.name: nothing-held-is-ever-undeclared
injections.why: a key outlives the job that wrote it and keeps its share of the budget; the workflows do not mention it and the API cannot know it is unwanted, so only holding both sides against each other finds it. R1123 moved WHERE that shows up — these bytes are inside the budget arithmetic now rather than a refusal of their own — so a reader that collected no orphans at all reports a smaller total than GitHub is holding

injections.name: the-range-is-the-tip-commit-alone
injections.why: THIS IS THE TREE THAT TURNED MAIN RED. Two commits went up in one push, the workflow moved in the first, and the gate asked `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD` — the tip had touched no hashed input, so eight jobs that had legitimately rebuilt from nothing were reported as a defect. Restoring it must turn the range law red and nothing else

injections.name: a-commit-that-is-not-in-the-checkout-is-diffed-from-anyway
injections.why: the runner names the commit a push started from whether or not the checkout fetched it, and diffing from a revision that is not here makes git fail — the gate then refuses to judge a repository that is fine, which is the same defect in the other direction

injections.name: the-workflow-stops-saying-where-the-push-began
injections.why: the program can only ask over the range if the runner is told to hand it over; the wiring is one line in a YAML file and nothing in the program notices its absence — the gate simply narrows back to the range that failed, silently

injections.name: the-checkout-goes-back-to-two-commits
injections.why: with the variable set and a shallow clone the gate narrows to HEAD~1..HEAD and says so — correct behaviour, and useless: the push range it was told about is not in the checkout, so the repair is only wired if BOTH halves are there. A depth that is a number is a guess about how many commits somebody pushes

injections.name: a-saved-key-is-a-cold-build
injections.why: R1102 — THE SENTENCE THAT WAS FALSE. `actions/cache` saves whenever the PRIMARY key missed, and `restore-keys` can have served an earlier generation to that same job; asserting a cold build from the save alone is the reading that deleted a 7.5 GB cache which was saving ten minutes, and this gate's own message agreed with it

injections.name: an-empty-disk-beside-a-held-generation-is-not-a-finding
injections.why: the cost the whole budget exists to buy off, and it is invisible on either instrument alone: storage says an archive is there, `cache-hit` says false for a prefix match either way, and only the job's own disk says nothing arrived. It is also what a mis-ordered pair of measuring steps looks like

injections.name: any-warmth-is-an-empty-disk
injections.why: the other direction of the same law: a gate that refuses every job regardless of what it received is one that fires on a repository doing nothing wrong, and a refusal nobody can act on is one somebody switches off

injections.name: the-archive-this-run-saved-was-one-it-could-have-restored
injections.why: a job that missed its key writes a new archive in its post step, so by the time this gate asks the API that archive heads the prefix — counting it makes every genuinely cold first run of a key look like a job that ignored a cache that was there

injections.name: only-the-newest-generation-could-have-been-restored
injections.why: `restore-keys` matches a PREFIX, so a superseded generation is one GitHub would have served; reading only the newest asks whether the archive this run just wrote was available to the job that wrote it

injections.name: a-flags-value-is-the-tree-to-judge
injections.why: `-- --restored rustc-log` under a reader taking the first word not beginning with `--` judges a repository rooted at `rustc-log`, finds no workflow, and refuses for a reason with nothing to do with any cache — and in the workflow file the mistake looks exactly like what was meant

injections.name: the-gate-judges-storage-alone
injections.why: both halves of the wiring are green-looking when absent: with no download step the directory is empty and every job reads as `did not say`, and with no flag the gate never looks. Either way the verdict that would have contradicted Round 1099 is the one that is suppressed

injections.name: every-silence-is-a-job-that-withheld-something
injections.why: R1107 — the sentence this repair is about. `replay` is an owner whose record is written in another workflow that uploads nothing, and the report named it as a job that `did not say what it started from`: a reader acting on that goes and wires a measurement into a workflow where the file dies with its runner, which is exactly the repair R1106 established must not be made

injections.name: reach-does-not-ask-what-a-workflow-collects
injections.why: a record is a file on a runner that is destroyed when the job ends, and only an upload step carries it out — a gate that never asks whether a workflow uploads anything reports the unhearable as the withheld

injections.name: reach-does-not-ask-which-run-this-is
injections.why: artifacts belong to a run, so a job of another workflow cannot be heard here however carefully it records — a gate that forgets it accuses that job of silence the day the other workflow starts uploading

injections.name: the-nearer-reason-is-printed-first
injections.why: an owner in another workflow that also collects nothing is both, and the two sentences send a reader to different places: one says a cross-run reader would hear it, the other says nothing will ever hear it. Printing the weaker one is how the wasted repair gets commissioned

injections.name: the-reading-about-who-can-be-heard-is-checked-against-nothing
injections.why: every sentence about whose silence is whose rests on which workflows collect, so a reader returning an empty set explains all eight owners with a reason nobody wrote — self-consistent and entirely wrong. A record actually in hand is the one observation that reading cannot argue with

injections.name: every-workflow-collects-something
injections.why: the exemption swallowing nothing: if every tracked workflow read as collecting, no owner would ever be beyond this gate's reach and the whole distinction would be decoration that never fires

injections.name: no-workflow-collects-anything
injections.why: the other direction, and the one that looks like an explanation: if nothing read as collecting, every owner would be reported unhearable and the gate would have stopped asking anybody for anything — an exemption that has swallowed its population

injections.name: a-nested-prefix-is-harmless-whatever-the-other-cache-holds
injections.why: R1122: `restore-keys` matches over the WHOLE repository's storage, and six of this file's keys sit under `Linux-cargo-`. For five that is harmless and is what the mechanism is FOR — they hold exactly the two cargo-home trees `validate` holds, so falling back onto one of their generations gets it the paths it asked for. Dropping the subset test reports all six, which is a reading that cannot tell the mechanism working from the mechanism landing 8.90 GB of somebody else's build directory

injections.name: only-an-identical-prefix-reaches-another-cache
injections.why: the other direction, and it is the one that answers NOTHING and looks clean: a fallback is a PREFIX match, so a reader comparing the two prefixes for equality finds no pair in any repository that has ever existed — the empty answer wearing the shape of a tidy one

injections.name: a-fallback-that-reaches-another-cache-is-not-refused
injections.why: R1123: the reading existed and nothing acted on it — which is the shape R1116 found in `restore-keys` itself, a property declared and compared never. An archive unpacks AS IT WAS STORED, so a job whose primary key misses lands a tree `path:` cannot stop and nothing in the census measures

injections.name: a-fallback-is-read-in-both-directions
injections.why: a prefix is not symmetric — the inner cache's key is longer, so it falls back onto nothing of the outer one's. Reporting the pair without direction refuses the tree twice and sends the reader to rename whichever key they read first, which is the one that was already fine

injections.name: an-archive-nothing-declares-costs-the-budget-nothing
injections.why: R1123 moved these bytes from a refusal of their own INTO the arithmetic, and this is the direction that move must not lose: a repository whose declarations fit only because the archives nobody declares were left out of the sum is over budget, and GitHub will evict something real to make room

injections.name: an-archive-nothing-declares-is-refused-on-its-own
injections.why: the direction R1122 was blocked by: a categorical refusal makes every RENAME red for the seven days the old archive takes to age out, so the gate refuses a repository for repairing itself — and renaming is the only repair for a key whose fallback reaches another cache's archive
